officialTitle: Prophylactic cranial irradiation versus observation in patients with extensive-disease small-cell lung cancer: a multicentre, randomised, open-label, phase 3 trial
setting: Extensive-stage SCLC responding to platinum doublet, no brain metastases on MRI

design.sampleSizeSourceQuote: Between April 3, 2009, and July 17, 2013, 224 patients were enrolled and randomly assigned (113 to prophylactic cranial irradiation and 111 to observation).
design.notes: MRI-confirmed absence of brain metastases at entry and scheduled brain MRI surveillance in both arms. Stopped early for futility at a planned interim analysis.

sponsor: Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare of Japan
clinicalQuestion: With MRI-confirmed absence of brain metastases and regular MRI surveillance, does prophylactic cranial irradiation improve overall survival in extensive-stage SCLC responding to chemotherapy?

pico.population: Extensive-disease SCLC with any response to platinum-based doublet chemotherapy and no brain metastases on MRI
pico.intervention: Prophylactic cranial irradiation (25 Gy in ten fractions)

arms.label: PCI
arms.dosing: 25 Gy in ten daily fractions of 2.5 Gy
arms.doseSourceQuote: randomly assigned (1:1) to receive prophylactic cranial irradiation (25 Gy in ten daily fractions of 2·5 Gy) or observation

publications.title: Prophylactic cranial irradiation versus observation in patients with extensive-disease small-cell lung cancer: a multicentre, randomised, open-label, phase 3 trial.
publications.label: Final analysis

outcomes.sourceQuote: In the final analysis, median overall survival was 11·6 months (95% CI 9·5-13·3) in the prophylactic cranial irradiation group and 13·7 months (10·2-16·4) in the observation group (hazard ratio 1·27, 95% CI 0·96-1·68; p=0·094).

safety.description: Grade 3 or worse anorexia at 3 months
safety.sourceQuote: The most frequent grade 3 or worse adverse events at 3 months were anorexia (six [6%] of 106 in the prophylactic cranial irradiation group vs two [2%] of 111 in the observation group)

safety.description: No treatment-related deaths in either group
safety.sourceQuote: No treatment-related deaths occurred in either group.

strengths: Randomised phase III design with MRI-confirmed absence of brain metastases at entry
Protocol-mandated MRI surveillance in both arms
limitations: Stopped early for futility, reducing precision
Conducted only in Japan; generalisability to other populations and to the immunotherapy era is uncertain

clinicalImplications.text: With MRI-confirmed absence of brain metastases and regular MRI surveillance, PCI did not prolong survival in extensive-stage SCLC, supporting MRI surveillance as an alternative to routine PCI.

tumourBoardPearl.text: MRI surveillance is only a valid alternative to PCI if it is actually delivered at regular intervals, as in this trial.

curation.notes: All numbers transcribed from the PubMed abstract of PMID 28343976.
